The source generator can't generate metadata for `ResponseError` because its `JsonConverter` (internal `Converter` class) doesn't have an accessible parameterless constructor. I need a different approach for `ResponseError`.

Since `ResponseError` has its own internal converter that the STJ source generator can't use, I need to handle it differently. I'll use `JsonSerializer.Serialize/Deserialize` with the default `JsonSerializerOptions` (which will pick up the `[JsonConverter]` attribute at runtime).

But wait - that would bring back the IL warnings. Instead, I should use `JsonSerializer.Serialize(writer, Error, (JsonTypeInfo<ResponseError>)ArmJsonSerializerContext.Default.Options.GetTypeInfo(typeof(ResponseError)))` or similar.
The cleanest solution is to remove `ResponseError` from the `[JsonSerializable]` context entirely and rely on its `[JsonConverter]` attribute at runtime, passing the context's `JsonSerializerOptions` to ensure consistency across all serialization. I need to check if Azure.Core provides its own `JsonSerializerContext` that I can leverage for `ResponseError` serialization in an AOT-compatible way, rather than trying to work around the internal converter.

data.reasoningText:
Two issues:
1. `ResponseInnerError` is also internal in Azure.Core - I need to handle inner errors differently
2. The source generator still can't generate metadata for `ResponseError` (SYSLIB1030) because it has an inaccessible converter

For issue 1, I'll skip inner error handling and just write/read it as raw JSON.
For issue 2, the `[JsonConverter(typeof(ResponseErrorConverter))]` on the class itself doesn't override the `[JsonConverter]` attribute on `ResponseError`. I need to put the converter in the `JsonSerializerOptions`.

Let me take a different approach. Instead of putting `ResponseError` in the `[JsonSerializable]` context (which doesn't work), I'll:
- Remove `ResponseError` from `ArmJsonSerializerContext` entirely
- Create a static `JsonSerializerOptions` with our custom converter added to the `Converters` collection
- Use that options object for all `ResponseError` serialization and deserialization, bypassing the source generator altogether
